git, run python3/awk arithmetic, run 'bash sweep.sh --md' (verify from the script first that

  - Layer 6's LAYER row and both geomeans (20.60x, 17.65x), the 5-node column

  - ssm_alpha+ssm_beta are 0.128% of layer 6's weights (the doc's Notes says 0.06%, wrong by

  - Report what CHECKS OUT as well as what does not. Populate verified_ok generously.
  - No speculation. If you cannot verify, mark it unverifiable and name the missing evidence.
  - Severity: critical = a headline number is wrong or the comparison is rigged; major = a
    real bias or a blocked reproduction; minor = imprecision that changes no conclusion;
    info = observation.


TARGETED VERIFICATION TASK

WHAT IS THE HONEST WHOLE-MODEL NUMBER? profiling_gemm_27b.md reports per-node speedups
up to 22.44x and layer geomeans of 20.60x / 17.65x, but never states an end-to-end prefill
speedup. Build the bound yourself:

     (48 SSM layers of the layer-6 shape set, 16 attention layers of the layer-7 set), plus
     the LM head / output projection. Find the LM head's shape (vocab x 5120) - check the
     model, the gguf, q1_0_* docs, or the repo's prior notes - and determine whether its row

 (b) Compute the model-wide MUL_MAT cycle total at 'pristine' and at 'd4' by weighting each

     LM head at whatever its gate outcome implies. Report the resulting whole-model MUL_MAT
     speedup and compare it to the headline 18.15x / 20.60x.
 (c) State clearly how much of the gap is (i) the un-repacked ssm tensors, (ii) the LM head,
     (iii) the choice of geometric over cycle-weighted mean.
 (d) Note explicitly that this still excludes all non-MUL_MAT work, so it is an upper bound.
This is the number a reader most needs and the document does not give it. Be careful and show
your arithmetic.

Report as findings + verified_ok.

1	# Bonsai-27B prefill: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node, SSM and attention layers
2	
3	The prefill/gemm counterpart of `profiling_gemv_27b.md`, which covers the same
4	27B nodes on the decode/gemv path. Same engine, same nodes, same four build
5	stages -- `nrows=4` instead of `nrows=2`.
6	
7	Generated 2026-08-31. Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one
8	MUL_MAT node; nothing here is inferred except layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows,
9	which are noted where they appear. Regenerate any table with
10	`MODEL=27b NODES="..." bash sweep.sh --md`.
11	
12	## Setup
13	
14	| | |
15	|---|---|
16	| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
17	| Model | `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen35, 64 layers, 3.80 GB, 1.125 bits/weight |
18	| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--no-mmap --mem-size 12G -t 1` |
19	| Path | prefill / gemm, `nrows=4` (asserted per leg from the `[roi]` line) |
20	| Layer mix | `full_attention_interval=4`: 48 SSM layers, 16 attention layers |
21	
22	Every layer in the model is one of two kinds, so measuring one of each covers
23	the whole model: **layer 6** is an SSM layer (48 of 64) and **layer 7** is an
24	attention layer (16 of 64).
25	
26	| name | flags | meaning |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
29	| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |
30	| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
31	| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
32	
33	## Layer 6 -- an SSM layer (48 of 64)
34	
35	| layer | node | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
36	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
37	| 6 | `attn_qkv` | 5120 x 10240 | 52,428,800 | 181,789,774 | 27,118,723 | 25,385,875 | 8,976,703 | 20.25x |
38	| 6 | `ssm_alpha` | 5120 x 48 | 245,760 | 936,969 | 939,289 | 939,798 | 938,688 | 1.00x |
39	| 6 | `ssm_beta` | 5120 x 48 | 245,760 | 949,957 | 947,611 | 947,471 | 945,595 | 1.00x |
40	| 6 | `attn_gate` | 5120 x 6144 | 31,457,280 | 109,087,879 | 16,595,177 | 15,548,729 | 5,708,128 | 19.11x |
41	| 6 | `ssm_out` | 6144 x 5120 | 31,457,280 | 122,621,082 | 17,362,812 | 16,461,292 | 6,500,681 | 18.86x |
42	| 6 | `ffn_gate` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,587,645 | 45,434,691 | 42,133,870 | 14,351,598 | 21.57x |
43	| 6 | `ffn_up` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,915,506 | 45,437,135 | 42,135,770 | 14,349,546 | 21.60x |
44	| 6 | `ffn_down` | 17408 x 5120 | 89,128,960 | 382,982,019 | 47,880,022 | 44,881,677 | 17,064,993 | 22.44x |
45	| | **LAYER** | | **383,221,760** | **1,417,870,831** | **201,715,460** | **188,434,482** | **68,835,932** | |
46	
47	Geometric mean over the layer's 6 optimizable nodes: **20.60x**. `ssm_alpha`
48	and `ssm_beta` are excluded from every average in this document, for the reason
49	given directly below.
50	
51	Per-stage speedup:
52	
53	| layer | node | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | **total** |
54	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
55	| 6 | `attn_qkv` | 6.70x | 1.07x | 2.83x | **20.25x** |
56	| 6 | `ssm_alpha` | 1.00x | 1.00x | 1.00x | **1.00x** |
57	| 6 | `ssm_beta` | 1.00x | 1.00x | 1.00x | **1.00x** |
58	| 6 | `attn_gate` | 6.57x | 1.07x | 2.72x | **19.11x** |
59	| 6 | `ssm_out` | 7.06x | 1.05x | 2.53x | **18.86x** |
60	| 6 | `ffn_gate` | 6.81x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.57x** |
61	| 6 | `ffn_up` | 6.82x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.60x** |
62	| 6 | `ffn_down` | 8.00x | 1.07x | 2.63x | **22.44x** |
63	
64	`ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` are the only two tensors in the model the kernel is
65	never applied to. The dispatch gate at `repack.cpp:4889` requires
66	`cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0` -- the row-parallel kernel puts 64 rows in 64 vector
67	lanes -- and both have 48 rows. The `if` is false, no repack happens, and all
68	four builds run the identical stock kernel, which is why their four cycle
69	counts agree to 0.3% and their speedup is exactly 1.00x. Nothing was applied,
70	so they measure nothing about the optimization and are left out of every
71	average here. They are 0.12% of the layer's weights; padding them to 64 rows
72	would bring them in.
73	
74	## Layer 7 -- an attention layer (16 of 64)
75	
76	| layer | node | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
77	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
78	| 7 | `attn_q` | 5120 x 12288 | 62,914,560 | 221,201,927 | 32,315,274 | 30,372,677 | 10,662,439 | 20.75x |
79	| 7 | `attn_v` | 5120 x 1024 | 5,242,880 | 18,582,438 | 3,434,839 | 3,268,543 | 1,630,251 | 11.40x |
80	| 7 | `attn_k` | 5120 x 1024 | 5,242,880 | 18,575,271 | 3,432,110 | 3,268,500 | 1,628,900 | 11.40x |
81	| 7 | `attn_output` | 6144 x 5120 | 31,457,280 | 119,759,239 | 17,118,167 | 16,275,722 | 6,337,136 | 18.90x |
82	| 7 | `ffn_gate` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,587,645 | 45,434,691 | 42,133,870 | 14,351,598 | 21.57x |
83	| 7 | `ffn_up` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,915,506 | 45,437,135 | 42,135,770 | 14,349,546 | 21.60x |
84	| 7 | `ffn_down` | 17408 x 5120 | 89,128,960 | 382,982,019 | 47,880,022 | 44,881,677 | 17,064,993 | 22.44x |
85	| | **LAYER** | | **372,244,480** | **1,380,604,045** | **241,152,929** | **225,336,152** | **66,024,863** | |
86	
87	Geometric mean over the layer's 7 nodes: **17.65x** -- lower than layer 6's
88	20.60x, but not for the same reason: layer 7 has no gate failures. It owns
89	`attn_v` and `attn_k`, the two 1024-row tensors that stop at 11.40x because the
90	per-call activation quantize dominates when there are only 16 row tiles to
91	spread it over.
92	
93	Layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows are the same tensor shapes as layer 6's and are
94	carried from them, exactly as `profiling_gemv_27b.md` does for decode. The
95	carry is sound: `ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` are themselves the same shape and were
96	measured **0.11%** apart at upstream and **0.01%** apart at `d4`.
97	
98	Per-stage speedup:
99	
100	| layer | node | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | **total** |
101	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
102	| 7 | `attn_q` | 6.85x | 1.06x | 2.85x | **20.75x** |
103	| 7 | `attn_v` | 5.41x | 1.05x | 2.00x | **11.40x** |
104	| 7 | `attn_k` | 5.41x | 1.05x | 2.01x | **11.40x** |
105	| 7 | `attn_output` | 7.00x | 1.05x | 2.57x | **18.90x** |
106	| 7 | `ffn_gate` | 6.81x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.57x** |
107	| 7 | `ffn_up` | 6.82x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.60x** |
108	| 7 | `ffn_down` | 8.00x | 1.07x | 2.63x | **22.44x** |
109	
110	## Where the prefill speedup comes from
111	
112	All figures are geometric means over nodes, with `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta`
113	excluded. Decode has only five nodes measured at all four stages, so the
114	head-to-head below uses **those same five on both sides** -- `attn_gate`,
115	`ssm_out`, `ffn_gate`, `ffn_up`, `ffn_down`:
116	
117	| step | 27B gemm (prefill) | 27B gemv (decode) |
118	|---|---:|---:|
119	| upstream to +repack | **7.04x** | 2.24x |
120	| +repack to +prefetch | **1.07x** | 1.60x |
121	| +prefetch to +vd4dots | **2.75x** | 3.54x |
122	| **total** | **20.67x** | **12.64x** |
123	
124	Over prefill's full set of 10 optimizable nodes the totals are 6.62x / 1.06x /
125	2.58x = **18.15x**, against decode's 10-node figure of 12.20x.
126	
127	Per layer:
128	
129	| | gemm | gemv |
130	|---|---:|---:|
131	| layer 6 (SSM), 6 nodes | **20.60x** | 12.53x |
132	| layer 7 (attention), 7 nodes | **17.65x** | 12.17x |
133	
134	Layer 7 is lower on both paths because it owns the two 1024-row tensors.
135	
136	This reproduces the 4B prefill result (6.11x / 1.04x / 2.46x) on a model 6.5x
137	larger with a different architecture. Prefill takes its win from the **layout**;
138	decode takes its win from **prefetch and the dot instruction**.
139	
140	The absolute cycles show it without any ratio. On `ffn_gate` at `+repack`:
141	
142	| path | tokens | cycles | per token |
143	|---|---:|---:|---:|
144	| decode | 2 | 73,356,044 | 36,678,022 |
145	| prefill | 4 | **45,434,691** | **11,358,673** |
146	
147	Prefill does twice the tokens in 62% of the cycles -- 3.2x cheaper per token --
148	because the gemm loads each weight vector once and fires four dots against it
149	(`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`), while the gemv reloads it per token.
150	
151	## Why prefill loses its edge on small tensors: a scalar activation quantizer
152	
153	Measured on Bonsai-4B, whose layer-7 nodes `attn_q`, `attn_v`, `attn_k`,
154	`ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` all share `ne0 = 2560` and differ only in row count, so
155	a node's cost splits cleanly into a per-call constant and a per-64-row-tile
156	term. Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%):
157	
158	| | fixed per call `F` | per tile `T` | per tile **per token** |
159	|---|---:|---:|---:|
160	| gemv `d4` (2 tok) | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
161	| gemm `d4` (4 tok) | 489,581 | 23,036 | **5,759** |
162	
163	In steady state the gemm is **1.88x more efficient per token**, exactly as the
164	M-tile sharing predicts. But it carries **12.4x the per-call fixed cost**, and
165	that constant is what decides the small nodes: `F` is 59% of 4B `attn_v`'s
166	total and only 12% of its `ffn_gate`. The same mechanism is why 27B `attn_v`
167	and `attn_k` stop at 11.40x while every larger node reaches 18.9-22.4x.
168	
169	`F` is not part of the kernel. Fitting the same model to every repack variant:
170	
171	| variant | gemm `F` | gemm `T` | gemv `F` | gemv `T` |
172	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
173	| `baseline` | 398,003 | 80,915 | 13,379 | 133,082 |
174	| `prefetch` | 441,355 | 76,544 | 27,294 | 85,084 |
175	| `d4` | 489,581 | 23,036 | 39,491 | 21,638 |
176	
177	`T` collapses 3.5x (gemm) and 6.2x (gemv) as the kernel improves; `F` stays put,
178	and stays an order of magnitude apart between the two paths. It is the shared
179	activation path, and the source says what it is. `forward_mul_mat` quantizes
180	activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`), and the routine it
181	picks depends on the token count:
182	
183	- **4 tokens** (`ne11 - ne11 % 4 == 4`) take
184	  `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>`, which selects
185	  `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` -- a **pure scalar** loop
186	  (`repack.cpp:51`, its own comment says `// scalar`): per 32-column block, 128
187	  `fabsf` for the amax scan plus 128 `roundf` plus the de-interleave index
188	  arithmetic. Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
189	  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
190	- **2 tokens** are not a multiple of 4, so they fall through to `from_float` =
191	  `quantize_row_q8_0`, which **is** RVV-vectorized on RISC-V
192	  (`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`).
193	
194	So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the
195	whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap, and at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest
196	single item in a small prefill matmul -- bigger than the kernel it feeds.
197	Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win.
198

200	
201	| layer | node | prefill | decode |
202	|---|---|---:|---:|
203	| 6 | `attn_qkv` | **20.25x** | 12.03x |
204	| 6 | `ssm_alpha` | 1.00x | 1.00x |
205	| 6 | `ssm_beta` | 1.00x | 1.00x |

208	| 6 | `ffn_gate` | **21.57x** | 12.11x |
209	| 6 | `ffn_up` | **21.60x** | 12.11x |
210	| 6 | `ffn_down` | **22.44x** | 14.30x |
211	| 7 | `attn_q` | **20.75x** | 11.82x |
212	| 7 | `attn_v` | 11.40x | 11.24x |
213	| 7 | `attn_k` | 11.40x | 11.25x |
214	| 7 | `attn_output` | **18.90x** | 12.61x |
215	
216	## Notes
217	
218	- **`ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` get nothing on prefill either.** All four builds
219	  land within 0.3% (936,969 / 939,289 / 939,798 / 938,688). 48 rows fails the
220	  repack gate `ne1 % 64 == 0`, so every build runs the identical stock kernel.
221	  They are 0.06% of the layer's weights but **2.7% of its optimized cycles** --
222	  the same over-weight dead spot decode has, and worse in relative terms because
223	  everything around them got 20x faster. Padding them to 64 rows is the cheapest
224	  win available on this model.
225	- **Total speedup tracks node size.** `attn_v`/`attn_k` (1024 rows) reach 11.40x
226	  while everything from 5120 rows up reaches 18.9-22.4x. On the small nodes
227	  prefill gains **no more than decode** (11.40x vs 11.24x). The section below
228	  decomposes why.
229	- **Upstream is exactly linear in tokens.** Measured on all 12 nodes: 1.97x to
230	  2.01x for 2x the tokens. `.nrows = 1` (`ggml-cpu.c:257`) means one `vec_dot`
231	  per (weight row, token), so there is no prefill kernel upstream at all.
232	- **Prefetch is worth slightly more here than on 4B** (1.05-1.08x vs
233	  1.03-1.05x). 27B tensors are far larger than the 2 MB L3, so more miss latency
234	  survives the M-tile reuse.
235	- **`ffn_down` is the best node on both paths** (22.44x prefill, 14.30x decode).
236	  Its K=17408 is the longest reduction dimension, which punishes upstream's
237	  per-32-column horizontal reduction hardest.
238	- **`ssm_out` and `attn_output` are the same shape** (6144 x 5120) and agree to

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cycle sweep over the whole (build variant x MUL_MAT node) grid, in parallel.
#
# measure.sh runs ONE node across a few variants, serially, straight to the
# terminal. This runs the grid: every variant against every node, many legs at
# once, one log per leg, so a killed or timed-out leg is re-run on its own
# without repeating the rest. The deliverable is the table --report prints.
#
#   bash sweep.sh                      # gemm/prefill, K=50..56, all 4 variants
#   MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh            # the decode path instead
#   NODES="51 56" VARIANTS="prefetch d4" bash sweep.sh
#   J=4 bash sweep.sh                  # 4 legs at a time (default 8)
#   bash sweep.sh --report             # re-print the table, run nothing
#   bash sweep.sh --selfcheck          # gate: reproduce two published numbers
#
# MODE picks the ggml path by picking the prompt, which is the ONLY thing that
# decides it (opt_roadmap F7, "MEASUREMENT GOTCHA"):
#   gemv  the warmup forward pass          -> nrows=2, decode kernel
#   gemm  --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt   -> nrows=4, pure prefill, no gemv tail
# The [roi] line reports nrows, and a leg whose nrows disagrees with MODE is
# recorded as BAD-NROWS instead of as a number. This matters more than it
# looks: the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and still prints a
# perfectly plausible cycle count, so the count alone can never catch it.
#
# Concurrency is safe: each hybrid run stages into its own make_temp_dir
# (andesim driver/manifest.cpp), and the cycle figure comes from a
# cycle-accurate RTL model, so host load cannot move it. --selfcheck proves
# both claims at once by running two legs together and comparing each against
# its published value.
#
# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz. A leg costs about 1 hour per 12M cycles,
# so the pristine ffn_* prefill legs are ~8 h each. Everything else is minutes.
set -u
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
# MODEL=4b|8b|27b picks the gguf AND the guest-RAM settings it needs. The big
# models do not fit the guest window mapped, so they need --no-mmap and a much
# larger --mem-size; getting this wrong does not error, it trap-storms.
#
# The resolved path goes in GGUF, NOT back into MODEL. MODEL arrives exported
# (`MODEL=27b bash sweep.sh`), so overwriting it with the path would re-export
# the path, and the `--leg` children xargs spawns would then resolve a
# DIFFERENT tag than their parent -- and so a different $OUT than the one the
# parent created.
TAG=${MODEL:-4b}
case "$TAG" in
  4b)  GGUF=$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf;  MEM=${MEM:-2000M}; MMAP=${MMAP-} ;;
  8b)  GGUF=$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf;  MEM=${MEM:-6G};    MMAP=${MMAP---no-mmap} ;;
  27b) GGUF=$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf; MEM=${MEM:-12G};   MMAP=${MMAP---no-mmap} ;;
  *)   GGUF=$TAG; MEM=${MEM:-12G}; MMAP=${MMAP---no-mmap}
       TAG=$(basename "$GGUF" .gguf) ;;
esac
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
MODE=${MODE:-gemm}
NODES=${NODES:-"50 51 52 53 54 55 56"}
VARIANTS=${VARIANTS:-"pristine baseline prefetch d4"}
J=${J:-8}
# Hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms. 24 h, because 12 h was NOT enough: the two
# largest upstream prefill legs (pristine ffn_up / ffn_down, ~83M and ~97M
# cycles) timed out at 12 h when the grid was running 16-wide. A timed-out leg
# costs its whole wall clock and yields nothing, so this is deliberately set
# well above the worst leg rather than close to it.
TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-86400000}
# Per model AND per path: the node index K means a different tensor in a
# different model, so 4B and 27B results must never share a directory.
# 4b keeps the original unsuffixed names so the existing sweeps still resolve.
OUT=${OUT:-$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE$([ "$TAG" = 4b ] || echo "-$TAG")}

case "$MODE" in
  gemm) PROMPT="The capital of France"; WARMUP="--no-warmup"; WANT_NROWS=4 ;;
  gemv) PROMPT="The capital of France is"; WARMUP="";         WANT_NROWS=2 ;;
  *) echo "MODE must be gemm or gemv (got '$MODE')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

bin_of() {  # $1 variant  $2 node -> the binary build.sh produced for that pair
  local suf=""; [ "$2" = 51 ] || suf="-k$2"
  printf '%s/bin-%s%s\n' "$LLAMA" "$1" "$suf"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one leg ---
# Runs to completion, leaves everything in the log. Never parses; --report is
# the single parser, so a leg re-run and a fresh report cannot disagree.
run_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  # Separate statements on purpose: bash expands every word of a `local` line
  # before it performs any of the assignments, so a log="...$v..." on the same
  # line would read an unset v.
  local v=$1 k=$2
  local log="$OUT/$v-k$k.log"
  local bin
  bin=$(bin_of "$v" "$k")
  # Own the directory rather than assume the parent made it: if the redirect
  # below fails the leg dies instantly having done nothing, and 12 of those
  # look exactly like a fast successful sweep.
  mkdir -p "$OUT"
  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
    echo "SKIP $v k=$k: no $bin (run: ROI_K=$k bash build.sh $v)" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  # Resume: a leg that already produced both lines is done. Anything else
  # (empty, truncated, timed out) is re-run.
  if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then
    echo "have $v k=$k"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "run  $v k=$k -> $log"
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
      --mem-size "$MEM" --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
      "$bin" -- -m "$GGUF" $MMAP -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) > "$log" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  grep -E '\[roi\] MUL_MAT|^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" | sed "s/^/    $v k=$k: /"
  [ $rc -eq 0 ] || echo "    $v k=$k: exit $rc" >&2
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ---
# One log -> "cycles<TAB>nrows<TAB>tensor<TAB>shape", or a reason it is not a
# number. Kept in awk so the nrows gate and the cycle read come from the same
# pass over the same file.
read_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  local log="$OUT/$1-k$2.log"
  [ -f "$log" ] || { printf 'MISSING\t\t\t\n'; return; }
  # [roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [2560 x 1024] nrows=4
  awk -v want="$WANT_NROWS" '
    /\[roi\] MUL_MAT/ {
      for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
        if ($i ~ /^src0=/)   { name = substr($i, 6) }
        if ($i ~ /^nrows=/)  { nrows = substr($i, 7) }
        if ($i ~ /^\[[0-9]+$/) { ne1 = $(i+2); sub(/\]$/, "", ne1)
                                 shape = substr($i, 2) "x" ne1 }
      }
    }
    /^\[andesim\] .* cycles/ { cyc = $2 }
    END {
      if (cyc == "")           { printf "PENDING\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      if (nrows != want)       { printf "BAD-NROWS\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", cyc, nrows, name, shape
    }' "$log"
}

report() {
  printf '%s sweep -- %s, %s, nrows=%s\n\n' "$MODE" "$(basename "$GGUF")" "$ENGINE" "$WANT_NROWS"
  # Header is built from VARIANTS so a partial sweep still lines up.
  printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' K tensor shape
  for v in $VARIANTS; do printf ' %14s' "$v"; done
  printf '\n'
  for k in $NODES; do
    local name="" shape="" cells=() f
    for v in $VARIANTS; do
      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
      cells+=("$cyc")
    done
    printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape"
    for f in "${cells[@]}"; do printf ' %14s' "$f"; done
    printf '\n'
  done
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- markdown ---
# The deliverable: the profiling_*.md table shape, generated from the logs so
# the document and the measurement can never drift apart. Reads the four
# stages BY NAME, so it does not care what order VARIANTS is in.
#   +repack    = upstream / baseline   (row-parallel 64x1 layout, F4)
#   +prefetch  = baseline / prefetch   (zicbop weight-stream prefetch, F7)
#   +vd4dots   = prefetch / d4         (nds.vd4dots.vv, F8+F9)
# A node missing any stage still prints its measured cells; only nodes with all
# four contribute to the geometric means, which is what "n =" reports.
md() {
  local k
  for k in $NODES; do
    local name shape cyc nrows nm sh v
    name=""; shape=""
    local -A c=()
    for v in pristine baseline prefetch d4; do
      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
      c[$v]=$cyc
    done
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape" \
      "${c[pristine]}" "${c[baseline]}" "${c[prefetch]}" "${c[d4]}"
  done | awk -F'\t' -v mode="$MODE" -v nr="$WANT_NROWS" -v eng="$ENGINE" '
    function num(x) { return (x ~ /^[0-9]+$/) }
    # Group digits by hand. printf "%%%'"'"'d" would need a locale that defines a
    # thousands separator; under LC_NUMERIC=C it silently prints plain digits.
    function comma(v,   s, o) {
      s = sprintf("%d", v); o = ""
      while (length(s) > 3) { o = "," substr(s, length(s) - 2) o
                              s = substr(s, 1, length(s) - 3) }
      return s o
    }
    function fmt(x) { return num(x) ? comma(x + 0) : x }
    function rat(a, b) { return (num(a) && num(b) && b+0 > 0) \
                                ? sprintf("%.2fx", a/b) : "-" }
    BEGIN {
      printf "| layer | node | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |\n"
      printf "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
      n = 0
    }
    {
      split($3, d, "x"); w = d[1] * d[2]
      # ggml names weights "blk.<layer>.<node>.weight"; the row reads as the
      # model sees it (which layer, which matmul), not as the harness does.
      # K, the graph-order index, is a measurement handle and stays out of it.
      split($2, t, ".")
      printf "| %s | `%s` | %s x %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n",
             (t[2] == "" ? $1 : t[2]), (t[3] == "" ? $2 : t[3]), d[1], d[2], comma(w),
             fmt($4), fmt($5), fmt($6), fmt($7), rat($4, $7)
      # Geo mean over the fully-measured nodes the kernel can actually be
      # applied to. A tensor whose row count is not a multiple of 64 fails the
      # repack dispatch gate (repack.cpp, `cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0`), so every
      # build runs the identical stock kernel on it and it scores exactly
      # 1.00x. Including such a node does not report a weak result, it reports
      # a result about a different kernel -- and a geometric mean is brutal to
      # values at 1, so two of them drag a 20x layer down to 9.7x. The row is
      # still printed; it just does not vote. Same test as the gate, not a
      # hand-kept list of names.
      skip = (d[2] % 64 != 0)
      if (skip && num($4) && num($7)) ng++
      if (!skip && num($4) && num($5) && num($6) && num($7)) {
        n++
        lr = log($4/$5); lp = log($5/$6); lv = log($6/$7)
        sr += lr; sp += lp; sv += lv
        if (n == 1 || lr < mnr) mnr = lr; if (n == 1 || lr > mxr) mxr = lr
        if (n == 1 || lp < mnp) mnp = lp; if (n == 1 || lp > mxp) mxp = lp
        if (n == 1 || lv < mnv) mnv = lv; if (n == 1 || lv > mxv) mxv = lv
        tu += $4; tb += $5; tp += $6; td += $7
      }
    }
    END {
      # Summed cycles per stage, but NO ratio: sum(upstream)/sum(vd4dots) is a
      # cycle-weighted aggregate, which the big nodes dominate and which reads
      # like a per-node speedup without being one. Speedup is reported as a
      # geometric mean over nodes, below, and only there.
      if (n) printf "| | **ALL %d** | | | **%s** | **%s** | **%s** | **%s** | |\n",
                    n, comma(tu), comma(tb), comma(tp), comma(td)
      printf "\n### Where the %s speedup comes from (n = %d nodes with all four stages)\n\n", mode, n
      if (ng) printf "%d node(s) excluded: rows not a multiple of 64, so the repack gate rejects them and every build runs the stock kernel.\n\n", ng
      printf "| step | geo mean | min | max |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
      if (n) {
        printf "| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
               exp(sr/n), exp(mnr), exp(mxr)
        printf "| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
               exp(sp/n), exp(mnp), exp(mxp)
        printf "| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
               exp(sv/n), exp(mnv), exp(mxv)
        printf "| **total** | **%.2fx** | | |\n", exp((sr+sp+sv)/n)
      }
      printf "\nengine %s, nrows=%d (%s path)\n", eng, nr, mode
    }'
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- selfcheck ---
# The harness gate. Two legs with values published in opt_roadmap (F8 for the
# prefetch build, F9 for the vd4dot one), run AT THE SAME TIME. Passing means
# the invocation measures what it claims AND that two concurrent hybrid runs
# do not disturb each other -- which is what licenses the parallel sweep.
selfcheck() {
  [ "$MODE" = gemm ] || { echo "--selfcheck has reference values for MODE=gemm only" >&2; exit 2; }
  mkdir -p "$OUT"
  run_leg prefetch 51 & local p1=$!
  run_leg d4       51 & local p2=$!
  wait $p1 $p2
  local rc=0 got
  # opt_roadmap F8: prefill K=51 prefetch 1,651,949 (an earlier session read
  # 1,649,275 on the same build -- 0.16% apart, so allow 1%).
  # opt_roadmap F9: prefill K=51 d4 818,314.
  for pair in "prefetch:1651949" "d4:818314"; do
    got=$(read_leg "${pair%%:*}" 51 | cut -f1)
    local want=${pair##*:}
    if [[ "$got" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && awk -v g="$got" -v w="$want" 'BEGIN{exit !(g>w*0.99 && g<w*1.01)}'; then
      printf 'PASS %-8s k=51 %s cycles (published %s)\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %-8s k=51 got %s, published %s\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
      rc=1
    fi
  done
  return $rc
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- main ---
# No argument = run the grid. Any UNKNOWN argument is an error, never a run:
# a mistyped flag used to fall through to the sweep and quietly start hours of
# simulation, which is the worst possible default.
case "${1:-}" in
  "")          ;;
  --report)    report; exit 0 ;;
  --md)        md; exit 0 ;;
  --selfcheck) selfcheck; exit $? ;;
  --leg)       run_leg "$2" "$3"; exit $? ;;   # internal: one xargs slot
  *) echo "usage: sweep.sh [--report|--md|--selfcheck]  (got '$1')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

[ -f "$GGUF" ] || { echo "no such model: $GGUF" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$OUT"
# Variant-major, in the order VARIANTS is given. xargs fills its slots from the
# front, so the slowest legs must be emitted first or they queue behind the
# fast ones and add their hours to the tail. `pristine` is ~6x every other
# variant on the same node, so emitting all of it first makes the wall clock
# the single longest leg instead of the sum.
for v in $VARIANTS; do for k in $NODES; do echo "$v $k"; done; done \
  | xargs -P "$J" -n 2 bash "$0" --leg
echo
report
